messages:
alex: Quick FYI — I started a soft-deprecation signal for api v1 (we need to migrate customers to v2). Wanted to get buy-in on who owns the shim fallback and what the signal payload looks like.

riley: +1 we should be explicit: separate "signal" (how we communicate deprecation) from the actual shim implementation. Signal should be tiny.

sam: propose header: `X-RW-Compat: v1;deprecate=2025-11-01;reason=param-shape`

maria: Agree header is fine, but also push an event to our telemetry pipeline so we can alert on unexpected upgrade failures.

alex: Example curl to illustrate signal:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-RW-Compat: v1;deprecate=2025-11-01" https://api.redwood.ai/generate
```

riley: For the shim: do we want gateway-level translation (fast, coarse) or runtime-side adapter (richer, more correct)? Tradeoffs: gateway = lower latency and isolated to eng-infra, runtime = deeper understanding of model contract.

sam: My vote: start with gateway-level shim for 80% of cases (header/body shape), and keep runtime adapter for stateful/semantic changes. Gateway shim can return `X-RW-Shim-Applied: true`.

maria: If gateway shim, who owns it? eng-infra for deployment, eng-platform for the compatibility rules (policy), eng-runtime for failing-safe behavior. Suggest: eng-platform owns the policy and telemetry, eng-infra owns the shim proxy, eng-runtime owns fallback behavior when shim can't handle a request.

alex: That split seems sane. I'll file a tiny ownership RFC and assign. Short checklist I want in the RFC: 1) signal schema, 2) shim header, 3) telemetry metrics, 4) rollout runbook, 5) SLA rollback conditions.

riley: Telemetry metrics to capture: `compat.signals.sent`, `compat.shim.applied`, `compat.shim.fallback_rate`, `compat.latency.delta`, `compat.error.regressions`. Also tag by tenant & route.

sam: Runbook notes: on >1% shim_fallback_rate for 24h -> rollback flagged; on >3% request failures after shim -> auto-disable shim for affected tenants. Ops to get page if failure burst.

maria: We should include a consumer opt-out header for customers who want to refuse shims: `X-RW-Compat-Optout: true`. If present, we must return 409 + explanatory body.

alex: Good catch. Also add a short grace period: Accept both shapes for 6 months post-signal, then 30-day notice before hard error. Add opt-in flag for early adopters.

eng-ops: Deploy bot: shim-proxy v0.1 scheduled to canary in us-west-2 at 2145006840. Will watch `compat.shim.applied` metric during canary.

riley: Quick example of gateway translation rule (pseudocode):
```
if header contains "v1" and route == /generate:
  transform payload: move `prompt_text` -> `input[0].text`
  set header `X-RW-Shim-Applied: true`
```

sam: We should persist a per-request shim trace id so runtime can correlate: `X-RW-Shim-Trace: <uuid>`; helpful for debugging.

maria: Decision summary so far (can we lock this in): 1) Signal via `X-RW-Compat` header + telemetry; 2) Gateway shim for surface transformations; 3) Runtime owns resilient fallback and hard-error enforcement; 4) eng-platform owns policy and rollout cadence; 5) eng-infra owns proxy deployment/flags.

alex: Let's lock it. I'll create the RFC + short migration checklist and tag owners. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary started (shim-proxy v0.1) — canary id c-2145 — monitoring `compat.shim.applied`.

eng-ops: Observability checklist posted in the RFC: queries for shim_applied, shim_fallback_rate, latencies. Will alert on thresholds Sam listed.

riley: One last thing — add a small header we can use for A/B: `X-RW-Compat-Mode: strict|shim|opt` so we can route per-tenant on the gateway.

alex: Perfect. End state: gateway honors `X-RW-Compat-Mode` if present; default is `shim` until hard deprecation date. I'll draft RFC now.
